card: This pull request centralizes the `trigger_reorg()` helper function in `blocktools.py` and removes local duplicates across functional tests. It also converts tests that simulated reorganizations using `invalidateblock` to realistic fork-based reorgs. This ensures tests exercise the actual chain-switching codepaths triggered by competing chains rather than manual block invalidation.
evidence: PR description: 'The remaining tests that still simulated reorgs with the invalidateblock RPC are converted to use them, since invalidateblock takes a different codepath than a reorg caused by a competing chain arriving.'
Follows up on merged PR #32587 ('test: Fix reorg patterns in tests to use proper fork-based approach').
problem: Multiple test suites duplicated the helper function used to submit fork blocks. Furthermore, several tests simulated reorgs by calling `invalidateblock`, which follows a different internal validation code path than a reorg triggered by the arrival of a competing chain.

risk.why: Touches only functional test framework helpers and test scripts.

scope_notes: Test framework cleanup and functional test adjustments across 13 test files.
summary: This pull request moves the `trigger_reorg()` helper method into `test_framework/blocktools.py` and removes duplicated copies across functional test scripts. It also converts several test suites from using `invalidateblock` RPC to realistic fork-based reorganizations using `create_empty_fork()` and `trigger_reorg()`.
